title: Proportion of population that has convenient access to public transport, by sex, age and persons with disabilities
graph_title: Percentage of households within 0-19 minutes' walk of a public transport stage
national_indicator_available: Percentage of households within 0-19 minutes' walk of a public transport stage
national_indicator_description: This indicator uses walking distance to the nearest public transport stage as a measure of convenient access to public transport.
computation_definitions: This indicator measures the percentage of households within 0-19 minutes' walk of the nearest public transport stage.
computation_calculations: Number of households within 0-19 minutes' walk of a public transport stage / Total number of households * 100
other_info: The data source also contains information on public transport usage rates, and on reasons for not using public transport (too far, poor quality service, no need, infrequent need, too expensive, other).
comments_limitations: This indicator uses walking distance as a proxy measure for convenient access to public transport. It does not account for other aspects of convenient access, such as cost; accessibility to special-needs customers; frequency of service; or comfort and safety in the transport environment. This indicator may be usefully supplemented by the other measures available in the data source. The global metadata for this indicator suggest a benchmark of 500 m distance from reference points for convenient access, whereas this measure includes walking distances of 0-19 minutes, which can be up to approximately 2 km in distance. Additionally, reflecting the evolving best practice in poverty measurement, a number of important methodological changes were made for EICV7 (2023-2024). Please see the linked data source for more information on methodology.
indicator_definition: Access to public transport is considered convenient when an officially recognized stop is accessible within a walking distance along the street network of 500 m from a reference point such as a home, school, work place, market, etc. to a low-capacity public transport system (e.g. bus, Bus Rapid Transit) and/or 1 km to a high-capacity system (e.g. rail, metro, ferry).
